about.title: What is MCP?
about.what: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard way for AI assistants to talk to an app. When it is on, LazyDM lets programs on this computer, like Claude Code, OpenAI Codex or OpenCode, look up and work with your notes.
about.use: Use it to ask an assistant to find a note, prepare a session, draft an enemy or tidy your links, using your real notes.
about.riskRead: Any program that has the token can read every note of the open Codex.
about.riskWrite: If you allow changes, an assistant can create and rewrite notes. Saves are conflict-checked and nothing is deleted unless you also allow deleting, but a wrong edit is still possible: keep a backup of your Codex.
about.riskInjection: Notes can come from other people through a shared folder. Text inside a note may try to steer the assistant.
about.moreTitle: Risks and what it is for

safe.title: Keep agents on MCP only
safe.why: The limits above apply to MCP. An assistant that can also edit files or run commands on this computer can write .md files in your Codex folder directly and skip them. That is controlled in the assistant, not in LazyDM.
safe.claude: In Claude Code, deny file edits in the Codex folder, in ~/.claude/settings.json, and keep shell commands on ask-first:
safe.codex: In OpenAI Codex, start it read-only, in ~/.codex/config.toml (or with --sandbox read-only):
safe.limits: A deny rule does not stop every shell command, and nothing here replaces a backup of your Codex.
safe.opencode: In OpenCode, ask before every edit and refuse the ones in the Codex folder, in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json:

delete.label: Allow deleting
delete.hint: Lets assistants send notes and sub-folders to the Trash. Nothing is deleted for good, and campaigns are never touched. Off by default.
delete.confirmDescription: They will be able to send notes, assets and sub-folders to the Trash, and links to them become plain text. You can restore them from the Trash. If your Codex is in a synced folder, your other devices will see them disappear at once.

about.title: How it works
about.what: This is a markdown file, agents.md, in the folder of this campaign. You write it: it tells AI assistants how you want your notes written and formatted. LazyDM never fills it in.
about.how: Write plain instructions, for example the language and tone of your notes, how to name things, which template or sections to use, what to link, and what to leave out. Short and concrete works best.
about.noMcp: Assistants that use the LazyDM MCP server read this file by themselves before they write. If you use an assistant without MCP, tell it to read this file, for example in its own instructions file.

welcome.lead: Prepare your campaign and run it at the table from the same desktop app. Lazy by design: sensible defaults and short paths keep preparation moving and table tools close.

prepare.title: Prepare at your desk
prepare.text: Write scenes, enemies, places and maps as linked notes. Rename a note and LazyDM updates the links to it.

session.title: Run at the table
session.text: When play begins, the campaign is already in front of you: initiative, hit points and maps sit next to your notes.

files.title: The campaign stays yours
files.text: Everything is Markdown in a folder of your choice, compatible with other tools. No account, no lock-in.

vault.where: It can live on this device, or in a cloud folder (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Box or Google Drive) to use it on more devices.
vault.cloudNote: In a cloud folder your cloud app does the syncing. LazyDM waits for pending downloads at start and warns you if two devices changed the same note.
